reference.title: Renal cell tumour subtypes (WHO 5th edition)
reference.intro: WHO 5th edition (2022) groups renal cell tumours into morphologically defined entities and molecularly defined RCC. Pair H&E architecture with targeted IHC (CAIX, CK7, CD117, AMACR, GATA3, FH/2SC, SDHB, TFE3) when clear or eosinophilic patterns overlap.
reference.note: Photomicrographs are from Wikimedia Commons under open Creative Commons licences. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma
points: Solid nests, acini and alveolar architecture with a delicate branching sinusoidal capillary network ('chicken-wire' vessels).
Diffuse strong membranous (box-like) CAIX, PAX8+, CD10+, RCC+, and usually CK7-negative (focal CK7 may appear in high-grade or cystic areas).
Distinguish from clear cell papillary RCT (cup-like CAIX, diffuse CK7+, apical nuclei) and TFE3-rearranged RCC (CAIX-negative/focal, TFE3+).

links.label: ExpertPath: Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma

images.caption: Clear cell RCC: nests of optically clear polygonal cells separated by a delicate branching capillary network.

groups.heading: Papillary renal cell carcinoma
points: WHO 5th edition no longer requires Type 1 / Type 2 subclassification; classic papillary RCC shows fibrovascular cores, foamy macrophages and psammoma bodies.
Typically CK7+, AMACR+, PAX8+, and CAIX-negative (except focal perinecrotic staining).
High-grade eosinophilic papillary tumours warrant screening for FH-deficient RCC (FH loss, 2SC+) or TFE3-rearranged RCC.

images.caption: Papillary RCC: true fibrovascular papillae lined by cuboidal cells with foamy histiocytes in the cores.

groups.heading: Chromophobe RCC vs renal oncocytoma
points: Chromophobe RCC: classic pale plant-like cells and/or eosinophilic cells with wrinkled 'raisinoid' nuclei, binucleation and perinuclear haloes; diffuse membranous CD117+ and diffuse strong CK7+.
Renal oncocytoma (benign mimic): nested eosinophilic cells in oedematous/hyalinised stroma with uniform round nuclei and central nucleoli; CD117+ but CK7-negative or only scattered single cells.
Chromophobe RCC is NOT graded by the WHO/ISUP nucleolar grading system.

images.caption: Classic chromophobe RCC: pale polygonal cells with sharp plant-like cell membranes and perinuclear haloes.
Eosinophilic chromophobe RCC: wrinkled raisinoid nuclei with perinuclear clearing; confirm with diffuse CK7 and CD117.
Renal oncocytoma (benign mimic): nested eosinophilic cells with regular round nuclei; CK7 is negative or only focal.

groups.heading: Clear cell papillary renal cell tumour
points: Renamed 'tumour' (indolent behaviour) in WHO 5th edition; never graded by WHO/ISUP.
Low-grade clear cells arranged in tubules and papillae with nuclei lined up apically away from the basement membrane ('piano-key' arrangement).
Characteristic immunoprofile: diffuse strong CK7+, cup-shaped (basolateral) CAIX+, GATA3+, AMACR-negative, CD10-negative.

links.label: ExpertPath: Clear Cell Papillary Renal Cell Tumour

images.caption: Clear cell papillary renal cell tumour: low-grade clear cells with apically aligned nuclei away from the basement membrane.

groups.heading: Molecularly defined & high-grade RCC
points: TFE3-rearranged and TFEB-altered RCC: clear/eosinophilic papillary or biphasic tumours with psammoma bodies or basement membrane globules; confirm by FISH/RNA fusion.
FH-deficient RCC: aggressive papillary/tubulocystic tumour with prominent inclusion-like eosinophilic nucleoli and perinucleolar haloes; loss of FH, strong 2SC+.
SDH-deficient RCC: uniform eosinophilic cells with flocculent intracytoplasmic vacuoles/inclusions; loss of SDHB.
Collecting duct carcinoma & SMARCB1-deficient renal medullary carcinoma: infiltrative high-grade medullary tumours with desmoplasia; check INI1/SMARCB1 loss and sickle cell trait.

fields.label: WHO/ISUP Grade
fields.default: G2: Nucleoli conspicuous and eosinophilic at 400x, visible but not prominent at 100x
options: G1: Nucleoli absent or inconspicuous and basophilic at 400x
G2: Nucleoli conspicuous and eosinophilic at 400x, visible but not prominent at 100x
G3: Nucleoli conspicuous and eosinophilic at 100x
G4: Extreme nuclear pleomorphism, multinucleated giant cells, and/or rhabdoid and/or sarcomatoid differentiation

reference.title: WHO/ISUP nucleolar grading (Grades 1–4)
reference.intro: Assign the highest WHO/ISUP grade present across the tumour (a single high-power field suffices). Validated for clear cell RCC and papillary RCC; do not apply to chromophobe RCC.
reference.note: Photomicrographs are from Wikimedia Commons under open Creative Commons licences. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Grades 1 and 2 (400x nucleolar assessment)
points: G1: Nucleoli are absent or inconspicuous and basophilic at 400x magnification.
G2: Nucleoli are conspicuous and eosinophilic at 400x magnification, and visible but not prominent at 100x magnification.

links.label: ExpertPath: WHO/ISUP Grading of Renal Cell Carcinoma

images.caption: Low-grade clear cell RCC (G1–G2): small uniform nuclei with absent or inconspicuous nucleoli at medium power.

groups.heading: Grade 3 (100x prominent eosinophilic nucleoli)
points: G3: Nucleoli are conspicuous and eosinophilic already at 100x magnification.
Ensure nucleoli are evaluated in well-fixed, non-necrotic areas.

links.label: ExpertPath: WHO/ISUP Grading of Renal Cell Carcinoma

images.caption: High-grade clear cell RCC (G3): enlarged nuclei with prominent cherry-red eosinophilic nucleoli easily seen at 100x.

groups.heading: Grade 4 (pleomorphism, sarcomatoid or rhabdoid)
points: G4: Tumour giant cells, extreme nuclear pleomorphism, sarcomatoid differentiation, and/or rhabdoid differentiation.
Any amount of sarcomatoid or rhabdoid differentiation automatically assigns Grade 4.

links.label: ExpertPath: Sarcomatoid and Rhabdoid Renal Cell Carcinoma

groups.heading: Tumours NOT graded by WHO/ISUP
points: Select 'Not applicable' for chromophobe RCC (nuclear atypia is intrinsic and does not correlate with outcome).
Select 'Not applicable' for clear cell papillary renal cell tumour and multilocular cystic renal neoplasm of low malignant potential.

reference.title: Sarcomatoid and rhabdoid differentiation
reference.intro: Sarcomatoid and rhabdoid features represent high-grade dedifferentiation across any RCC subtype, automatically confer WHO/ISUP Grade 4, and must be reported with an estimated percentage (CAP 4.3.0.0).
reference.note: ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Sarcomatoid differentiation
points: Malignant spindle cell proliferation resembling a pleomorphic or fascicular sarcoma (any amount qualifies; no minimum percentage).
Always assigns WHO/ISUP Grade 4 even if seen in chromophobe RCC.
Report the underlying epithelial subtype when identifiable (e.g. clear cell RCC with sarcomatoid features) and estimate the percentage.

groups.heading: Rhabdoid differentiation
points: Sheets or clusters of large discohesive epithelioid cells with eccentric vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli and large paranuclear eosinophilic cytoplasmic globules.
Automatically assigns WHO/ISUP Grade 4; estimate the percentage of the rhabdoid component.

fields.label: Tumour extension (pT)
options: Renal vein or its segmental branches
Vena cava above diaphragm or invading vena cava wall
Beyond Gerota's fascia (including contiguous ipsilateral adrenal gland)

reference.title: pT3a–pT4 anatomic landmarks (renal sinus, fat, vein, adrenal)
reference.intro: Careful sampling of the renal sinus interface is the single most common source of pT3a upstaging in RCC because no fibrous capsule separates the renal cortex from the renal sinus fat.
reference.note: ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Renal sinus fat and pelvicalyceal system (pT3a)
points: Renal sinus invasion (pT3a): direct contact of tumour with renal sinus fat or loose connective tissue containing muscular venous branches, OR invasion of any endothelial-lined space within the renal sinus.
Pelvicalyceal invasion (pT3a): tumour breaks through the urothelial basement membrane into the calyceal or pelvic lumen.

links.label: ExpertPath: Staging of Renal Cell Carcinoma

groups.heading: Perinephric fat and venous invasion (pT3a vs pT3b/pT3c)
points: Perinephric fat (pT3a): tumour breaches the renal capsule to touch perinephric adipocytes (do not upstage for bulging into an intact fibrous pseudocapsule).
Renal vein / segmental branches (pT3a): tumour within any muscular-walled renal venous branch (gross or microscopic).
IVC below diaphragm = pT3b; IVC above diaphragm OR direct invasion of the vena cava wall = pT3c.

links.label: ExpertPath: Staging of Renal Cell Carcinoma

groups.heading: Gerota's fascia and ipsilateral adrenal gland (pT4 vs pM1)
points: Contiguous direct extension beyond Gerota's fascia, including direct invasion into the ipsilateral adrenal gland = pT4.
Non-contiguous (haematogenous) metastasis to the ipsilateral adrenal gland = pM1, NOT pT4.

reference.title: Nephrectomy surgical margins (partial vs radical)
reference.intro: Relevant margins depend on whether the specimen is a partial or radical nephrectomy. Ink the parenchymal bed and capsular surface before sectioning.
reference.note: ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Partial nephrectomy margins
points: Evaluate the inked renal parenchymal resection margin (distance in mm if clear; tumour on ink = positive) and the perinephric fat / capsular margin.
A thin intact fibrous pseudocapsule at ink without tumour cells touching ink is reported as uninvolved (closest < 1 mm).

links.label: ExpertPath: Kidney Specimen Handling and Margins

groups.heading: Radical nephrectomy margins
points: Evaluate the renal vein margin (en face — check for tumour thrombus adherent to or extending to the stapled/transected vein edge), ureteral margin, perinephric fat / Gerota's fascia soft tissue margin, and renal sinus soft tissue margin.
